title: Background runs on a second account
summary: A separate account for background work, a fail-closed route to it, the spawn helper, lanes, a driver lane and an inbox responder.
why: Background runs can spend a whole subscription overnight. Routing them through one guarded helper on their own account keeps that spend visible, bounded and away from the account you type into.

items.title: Second account for background runs
items.does: Adds the rule that background runs use their own Claude config dir and subscription; the wizard creates the dir and opens a pane where you log in yourself.
items.why: Background spend must not bill the account you work in interactively, or a long night run can leave you without quota in the morning.

items.title: Loopback route contract
items.does: Adds the split-mode contract: background runs reach the second account through a proxy you run on a loopback address, checked before every run.
items.why: Split routing keeps your interactive login untouched. The profile names no proxy and ships none; it only checks the one you run.

items.title: Kill-switch user variable
items.does: Sets the user environment variable CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BASE_URL to your pinned proxy address; deleting it stops every next background run on the machine.
items.why: One act, deleting a variable, stops all background spend at once, even for processes already running.

items.title: Route file: split or single
items.does: Adds the rule that a route file chooses split or single mode and is read fresh before every run; the wizard's headless step writes it.
items.why: People with one account still need background runs that fail closed; single mode gives them that without a proxy.

items.title: The only background spawn path
items.does: Copies kit_headless.py and the rule that nothing else starts a background claude: route check, a daily run cap, lean flags, model choice, usage line and status file.
items.why: Every other path that started claude in the background ran unguarded, billed the wrong account or started far too many runs.

items.title: Usage line per background run
items.does: Adds the rule that each background run appends one usage line with its kind, label and route.
items.why: A weekly split of build work against note chatter needs data from every run; without it the cost question cannot be answered.

items.title: Lanes with their own worktrees
items.does: Copies kit_lanes.py: per-repository lane locks, one git worktree per lane and a machine-wide governor that shares three lanes fairly.
items.why: Several background runs over one working tree starved and overwrote each other.

items.title: Driver lane template
items.does: Installs driver_lane.py, which re-fires one unit of work per cycle through the spawn helper with a progress file, a halt file and a cycle cap.
items.why: Long work must be resumable, bounded and receipted, not one enormous run that either finishes or vanishes.

items.title: Inbox responder every 15 minutes
items.does: Installs inbox_responder.py and a task that runs it every 15 minutes: free classification, ledger lines for acknowledgements, one run for ORDER, FIX and RULING notes.
items.why: The inbox gets acted on automatically and unattended, at the lowest cost that still does the work.

items.title: Halt files pause loops
items.does: Adds the halt-file rule and the /done step that pauses the responder for the whole ritual.
items.why: A responder committing halfway through /done once left the hand-off and the commit out of step.

items.title: Background run contract
items.does: Installs /headless-run: the fixed prompt contract for one long background unit, with a merger, worktree agents, a verifier and its own /done fold.
items.why: Long autonomous runs need a fixed contract, or each one invents its own idea of finished.

items.title: Armed fallback after a weekly limit
items.does: Adds the armed-fallback rule: only when you arm it, a confirmed 7-day limit on one account moves the next runs to the other, one hop, logged.
items.why: Stalling a whole week because one account is spent is worse than one logged hop you chose in advance.
items.notes: The wizard writes the armed flag only after the typed acknowledgement apply hl-fallback-armed.
